Benchmarking the effect of attribute selection methods on the performance of classification algorithms in a study to diganose the chronic kidney disease (CKD) by using classification algorithms are aimed. Data set on CKD taken from the UCI machine learning repository has been used for the experiments. After a variety of pre-processing, normalization and attribute selection processes, classifier models are designed. In order to determine the attributes that have gerater contribution on the classification results, the Correlation Based attribute selection (CBAS) method and Fuzzy Rough Set Based attribute selection (FRSBAS) method were used. Two data sets obtained by each attribute selection method and the raw data are classified by 4 classifiers including k-Nearest Neighbor, Navie Bayes, Random Forest and Logistic Regression. The test and training data are separated by 5-fold cross validation. The accuracy, precision, sensitivity, ROC curve and F-measure parameters obtained from confusion matrix are used to compare and evaluate the results of the models. As a result of the study, it is seen that the application of FRSBAS method on CKD data set performs better in all classification algorithms.

title: Logo Image Dataset (LID): A Dataset of Trademark Images with Vienna Codes and Bounding Boxes for Logo Detection
venue: 2026 18th International Conference on Knowledge and Smart Technology (KST)
abstract: Logos are considered crucial for brands and businesses, and the development of logo recognition processes and brand identification processes is of particular interest, with the aim of leveraging artificial intelligence to enhance the efficiency of trademark management. Although recent deep learning-based object detection methods have demonstrated promising performance, their effectiveness is often limited by the lack of datasets that provide fine-grained spatial annotations. This paper presents the Logo Image Dataset (LID), a dataset of 7,463 real-world trademark images collected from publicly available sources commonly encountered in Thailand. Each image is manually annotated with object-level labels, bounding-box coordinates, and Vienna Classification codes describing figurative elements. Evaluated using a custom YOLO architecture, the model achieved a mAP at 0.5 IoU of 0.918 and a mAP across thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95 of 0.85. The results yielded a peak F1 score of 0.84 at a confidence threshold of 0.73. Analysis of confusion matrices indicates that residual errors mainly arise from visually similar geometric motifs and long-tailed classes. These results demonstrate that LID provides effective supervision for fine-grained logo detection and offers a practical foundation for automated trademark search and analysis systems.

title: Cops-Ref: A New Dataset and Task on Compositional Referring Expression Comprehension
authors: Zhenfang Chen; Peng Wang; Lin Ma; Kwan-Yee K. Wong; Qi Wu
venue: 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
abstract: Referring expression comprehension (REF) aims at identifying a particular object in a scene by a natural language expression. It requires joint reasoning over the textual and visual domains to solve the problem. Some popular referring expression datasets, however, fail to provide an ideal test bed for evaluating the reasoning ability of the models, mainly because 1) their expressions typically describe only some simple distinctive properties of the object and 2) their images contain limited distracting information. To bridge the gap, we propose a new dataset for visual reasoning in context of referring expression comprehension with two main features. First, we design a novel expression engine rendering various reasoning logics that can be flexibly combined with rich visual properties to generate expressions with varying compositionality. Second, to better exploit the full reasoning chain embodied in an expression, we propose a new test setting by adding additional distracting images containing objects sharing similar properties with the referent, thus minimising the success rate of reasoning-free cross-domain alignment. We evaluate several state-of-the-art REF models, but find none of them can achieve promising performance. A proposed modular hard mining strategy performs the best but still leaves substantial room for improvement.

title: Enhancing Automatic Readability Assessment with Verb Frame Features
authors: Tianyuan Cai; Ho Hung Lim; John S. Y. Lee; Meichun Liu
venue: 2022 International Conference on Asian Language Processing (IALP)
abstract: Patterns of verb usage, as encoded in verb frame elements, have been shown to correlate with text readability. While automatic readability assessment models have incorporated a wide range of features on lexical, syntactic, semantic and discourse properties of a text, none of these features directly exploit the semantic information provided in verb frames. This paper investigates whether features based on semantic frames can improve the performance of Chinese readability assessment models. We conduct experiments with manually annotated verb frame elements in Mandarin VerbNet, including the use of non-core frame elements, subject omission, metaphoric usage and clause as verb argument. Experimental results on a corpus of Chinese texts, spanning twelve school grades, show that these frame features significantly raise readability assessment accuracy over a baseline model that relies on surface features only.

title: Architecture exploration of QoS control Silicon Intellectual Properties for Cross-Layer Designs in wireless networks
authors: Chao-Lieh Chen; Li-Shin Chuo; Wu-Liang Cheng; Chun-Ching Wu; Chien-Hao Lai
venue: 2011 IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo
abstract: We propose an architecture exploration scheme for QoS control Silicon Intellectual Properties (SIPs). The scheme integrates network simulator (NS-2), embedded Linux operating system, Linux driver, Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools, extended on-chip bus, and real Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) hardware for comprehension of how data bus width and clock rate affect QoS performance in wireless networks. Software and hardware co-design flow and programming paradigm for evolving the FPGA prototype toward a platform-based reusable SIP with driver and cross-layer interface are also depicted. Three QoS control experiments in video streaming over HCCA, EDCA, and WiMAX wireless technologies demonstrate the proposed exploration scheme effectively helps engineers comprehend impacts of architectural design parameters on networking performances in wireless multimedia communications.

title: Multi-Perspective Cross-Modal Object Encoding for Referring Expression Comprehension
authors: Jingcheng Ke; Jie Wen; Huiting Wang; Wen-Huang Cheng; Jia Wang
abstract: Referring expression comprehension (REC) is a crucial task in understanding how a given text description identifies a target object within an image. Existing two-stage REC methods have demonstrated strong performance due to their rational framework design. However, during the encoding of object candidates in an image, most two-stage methods rely exclusively on features extracted from pre-trained detectors, often neglecting the contextual relationships between an object and its neighboring elements. This limitation hinders the full capture of contextual and relational information, reducing the discriminative power of object representations and negatively impacting subsequent processing. In this paper, we propose two novel plug-and-adapt modules: expression-guided label representation module (ELR) and cross-modal calibrated semantic module (CCS), designed to enhance two-stage REC methods. Specifically, the ELR module connects the noun phases of expression to the categorical labels of object candidates in the image, ensuring effective alignment between them. Guided by these connections, a CCS module is introduced to represent each object candidate by integrating its features with those of neighboring candidates from multiple perspectives. This preserves the intrinsic information of each candidate while incorporating relational cues from other objects, enabling more precise embeddings and effective downstream processing in two-stage REC methods. Extensive experiments on six datasets demonstrate the importance of incorporating prior statistical knowledge, and detailed analysis shows that the proposed modules strengthen the alignment between image and text. As a result, our method achieves competitive performance and is compatible with most two-stage methods in the REC task. The code is available on Github: https://github.com/freedom6927/ELR_CCS.git.

title: Performance Evaluation Of Classifiers For Analysis Of Road Accidents
authors: C. Sugetha; L. Karunya; E. Prabhavathi; P. Kola Sujatha
venue: 2017 Ninth International Conference on Advanced Computing (ICoAC)
abstract: Road accidents happen quite often nowadays. Some accidents result in severe injuries whereas few are fatal. The consequences have a great impact on society. Many analytical procedures have been carried out to determine the causes of road accidents. The objective of this analysis is to employ data mining techniques for determining the factors that influence road accidents. The paper also focuses on evaluating the performance of various classification model in predicting the severity of accidents and it is tested upon different types of datasets. The results can be used to choose the suitable classifier to use with various kinds of datasets.

title: Exploring the Relationships between Design Metrics and Package Understandability: A Case Study
venue: 2010 IEEE 18th International Conference on Program Comprehension
abstract: In object-oriented designs, packages represent important high-level organization units that group classes. This paper explores the relationships between five package-level metrics and the average effort required to understand a package in object-oriented design. These metrics measure different structural properties of a package such as size, coupling and stability. A case study was conducted using eighteen packages taken from two open source software systems. Correlation, collinearity, and multivariate regression analyses were performed. The results obtained from this study indicate statistically significant correlation between most of the metrics and understandability of a package.

title: Predicting Students Performance in Exams using Machine Learning Techniques
authors: Khanyisile Sixhaxa; Ashwini Jadhav; Ritesh Ajoodha
venue: 2022 12th International Conference on Cloud Computing, Data Science & Engineering (Confluence)
abstract: Predicting students success has been a very popular study across different fields and with this study we will be focusing on how Machine Learning can aid us in giving us insight in how students will perform in their exams. In this paper, we propose a model that takes in Demographic, Academic and Behavioural attributes and investigate the how these attributes contribute a student’s performance and also predict at risk students. For the analysis of the features we will use the Mutual Information algorithm, alongside five machine learning models that are a mixture of classification and regression classifiers. We will also use these models to predict our students performance. The five classifiers used in this study are as follows: Gaussian Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbour and Logistic Regression and we achieved prediction accuracy of 50.83%, 81.67%, 78.33%, 75.00% and 74.17% respectively. The results yielded revealed that there is a strong correlation between a student’s behavioural characteristics and their academic performance.

title: Utilizing Footstep Sound Event Detection by Using CNN Techniques for Assuring Property Security
abstract: The advanced camera systems developed for property security prove inadequate when faced with the ease of disabling the cameras. Therefore, incorporating sound data from potential threats can also play a significant role in ensuring property security. This sound event-based approach enables a more compact installation and allows for the use of affordable microphones, offering an alternative to visual-based security systems. We propose deep learning based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm for classification of footstep sound events. The study includes two consecutive stages: ReaLISED dataset and refined ReaLISED supported by Epidemic Sound data. Sound event files are transformed into Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and a CNN is fed with the represented images of MFCC. By optimizing the model parameters, our unique model detected footstep sound events with 98% accuracy among 17 other sound events. Validation through Repeated Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation (5 folds, 10 repetitions) and comparisons with state-of-the-art architectures demonstrated robust performance, with F1-Scores ranging from 0.905 to 0.992 and a mean of 0.960. The strategic incorporation of diverse open-source data fosters transparency and reproducibility, enhancing the model’s adaptability and reliability in handling real-world audio patterns, as evidenced by its commendable 1% error rate in precise identification.

title: Exploring non-destructive mechanical characterisation of hydrogels using hyperspectral imaging and machine vision
authors: Jean Henri Odendaal; Nitin Bhatia; Russell Wilson; Johan Potgieter
venue: 2022 28th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Hydrogel polymer networks are non-covalently crosslinked soft materials that exhibit unique mechanical and excellent bio-characteristics such as adapting to environmental forces and strengthening to the conditions they experience. Quantifying these characteristics are important for their usage in multitude of applications especially where new formulations or composites of hydrogels being prepared such as for 3D printing. Often such characteristics are quantified using destruc-tive methods and/or using complex mathematical models, which can destroy samples, are limiting and time-consuming. Herein, we describe non-destructive hyperspectral imaging (HSI) based machine vision approach that enable faster characterisation of hydrogel's mechanical properties. Several measurements of hydrogel samples were collected using HSI to develop a database used to train a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) based learning model. From the confusion matrix results, we observed the >90% accuracy, which we think can provide relatively good performance compared to other traditional methods. We conclude that HSI with machine vision could simplify the measurement procedure, allowing for a more straightforward characterisation of hydrogel samples, is fast and reproducible to provide serve as both an in-process and a quality control method.

title: Evaluating the Performance of Different Machine Learning Algorithms for Crop Recommendation
authors: Mudit Kumar; Parth Sharma; Radhika Pal; Preeti Saini; Supriya Shukla
venue: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: A significant portion of Indians view agriculture as their main source of revenue. Crop production is a significant industry in our nation. Applications of machine learning are changing the data processing and decisioning process that have a significant influence on the world economy. The natural nutrients or physiochemical characteristics of the soil aid in the understanding of the dynamics of the soil ecosystem by the researchers and are essential in assisting farmers in making daily choices. In order to forecast and evaluate soil properties and make better decisions on agricultural soil health management, our work focuses on closely examining and assessing machine learning (ML) methodologies.Machine learning has entered the picture with the introduction of big data technologies and high-performance computers, creating new opportunities for data-intensive research in the interdisciplinary field of agricultural technology. On the other hand, single-component soil property predictions were not as accurate. In the long run, combining these technologies can have revolutionized contemporary agriculture by raising crop yields and reducing waste. Helping someone cultivate crops successfully to obtain a high yield is the aim of this activity. Estimating enhanced crop output through the application of machine learning algorithms, which are utilized in crop yield estimates, is one of the challenging issues facing the agricultural sector. We have implemented the five supervised learning models. Random Forest give the best accuracy score of 97%.

title: Recognition-Memory Asymmetries Predicted by Individual Item Memorability
authors: Utochkin, Igor; Chiang, Nicholas; Bainbridge, Wilma A.
abstract: According to current recognition-memory theories, a major source of confusion when people judge which stimuli they remember is the contextual similarity of those stimuli to those from the studied list. However, these theories overlook the potential for confusions to arise from item-specific memorability properties not explained by list properties-namely, the likelihood that a stimulus will be correctly recognized if studied ("hittability") or falsely recognized if not ("false alarmability")-independent of contextual similarity. Here, we introduce a memorability continuum model based on signal detection theory. The model predicts that differences in the individual "hittability" and "false alarmability" of arbitrary Items A and B grounded in their representational locations on an internal familiarity axis can often lead to asymmetric recognition performance in a forced-choice task such that recognition of Target A over Foil B is more accurate than recognition of Target B over Foil A. In a forced-choice experiment testing memory for real-world object images, the model successfully predicted specific item pair asymmetries. Using deep convolutional neural networks validated on human similarity judgments, we showed that memory-list context explains only a small fraction of variance in false alarmability but not hittability. We also show that, while interitem similarity explains a small percentage of variance in their forced-choice discriminability, ignoring their differential memorability properties as targets and foils fails to predict the asymmetries. Our results highlight the need to integrate item-level memorability into existing recognition-memory theories.

title: Compound Fault Separation and Extraction of Gears Using Adaptive Correlated Kurtogram and Product Envelope Spectrum
authors: Peng, Yeping; Duan, Qiao; Kong, Desheng; Li, Junnan; Wu, Chao; Cao, Guang-Zhong
venue: IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON INSTRUMENTATION AND MEASUREMENT
abstract: With the increasing complexity of mechanical equipment, gear compound fault diagnosis faces severe challenges due to signal cross-coupling and strong noise interference. Existing compound fault separation methods suffer from prominent drawbacks including severe mode aliasing, cross-modulation confusion and erroneous band selection under complicated operating conditions, which greatly degrade the separation performance of multisource coupled fault signals. To this end, this article presents a novel method for separation and feature extraction of gear compound faults based on an adaptive correlated kurtogram (ACKgram) and product envelope spectrum (PES) is proposed. First, an adaptive frequency band partitioning strategy combining a 1/3 binary and fault feature-driven sliding window is constructed to identify resonant frequency bands, which eliminates spectral aliasing and information loss induced by the fixed partitioning in conventional resonance demodulation techniques. Second, correlated kurtosis of ES (CKES) is introduced to as the frequency band selection index to replace traditional kurtosis, which effectively avoids misjudgment caused by aperiodic random impulse interference and realizes accurate selection of optimal frequency band. Third, an empirical wavelet transform (EWT) filter bank is used to separate target fault components and restrain global mode aliasing. Finally, PES demodulation is implemented to amplify weak periodic fault signatures while suppressing irrelevant nonperiodic noise, taking full advantage of the synergistic properties of multichannel envelope spectra. Simulations and gearbox experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method extracts separated compound fault signatures. It achieves an envelope signal-to-noise ratio ${(\boldsymbol {SNR}}_{\boldsymbol {env}})$ improvement of 10-32 dB compared with raw signals, with an overall fault frequency recognition rate (FFRR) exceeding 0.935.

title: Predicting the Difficulty of Korean College Scholastic Ability Test Reading Comprehension Questions Using LLM-Based Qualitative Features
authors: Jo, Juhye; Cho, Seok Hyeon; Choi, Junhyeok; Yoon, Jeewhan; Han, Sung Won
abstract: Accurate estimation of item difficulty is essential to ensure fairness, reliability, and discriminative power in high-stakes standardized tests. However, existing approaches rely primarily on surface-level linguistic features or implicit representations learned by neural models, which may not explicitly capture the cognitive and reasoning processes underlying perceived difficulty. In this study, we propose a feature-based framework for predicting the difficulty of Korean College Scholastic Ability Test (KCSAT) reading comprehension items by integrating quantitative item features ( F-1 ) and large language model (LLM)-based qualitative features ( F-2 ). Although F-1 captures traditional linguistic and structural properties, F-2 is designed to quantify deeper aspects of item difficulty, including abstraction, logical complexity, cognitive load, and distractor effectiveness, using an LLM. Extensive experiments were conducted on KCSAT reading data collected from 2016 to 2024 under both time-based and stratified evaluation settings. The results indicate that feature-only models using F-1+F-2 achieve a performance comparable to, and in some cases, exceeding, that of models that utilize contextual textual embeddings. In the classification task, the proposed approach achieved a Macro F1-score of 0.6215 under a time-based split, highlighting the importance of temporal structure in difficulty prediction. Ablation studies further demonstrated that LLM-based features provide complementary information beyond traditional features, with different components contributing differently depending on the task. These findings indicate that structured feature representations, particularly those incorporating LLM-derived qualitative factors, provide an effective and interpretable approach for modeling item difficulty in high-stakes reading assessments.

title: Effects of Item Format, Language Family, and Orthographic System Typology on L2 Reading Comprehension
authors: Algeciras, Karen Martinez; Elosua, Paula; Gimenez, Javier Fruns
abstract: Ensuring score comparability constitutes a central issue in L2 reading comprehension assessment, particularly when multiple sources of variability may affect the interpretation of test results. Within this context, the present study examines the relationship between item format and specific L1 linguistic properties-such as orthographic transparency, typological family, and writing system-in order to analyze how performance varies as a function of these linguistic characteristics. To this end, data from 8,701 participants who took the DELE B2 certification examination were analyzed using repeated-measures linear mixed models. Speakers of transparent, alphabetic, and Indo-European languages tended to obtain higher scores, although the magnitude of these differences varied across task types. Multiple-choice and selective cloze formats accentuated some between-group differences, whereas rational cloze showed more homogeneous performance patterns. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between item format and performance varies according to L1 linguistic characteristics. The implications of these findings for score validity in multilingual contexts are discussed, highlighting the need to consider item format as a potential method factor.

title: Class-based Obfuscation with Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithms on Source Code
authors: Yang, Guan-Yan; Liu, Tsung-Han; Wang, Farn; Yeh, Kuo-Hui
abstract: With the proliferation of software, protecting intellectual property from reverse engineering has become a paramount concern. Malicious actors who successfully decipher program logic can replicate applications, inject malicious code, and compromise user security. Code obfuscation serves as a critical defense mechanism by transforming a program's structure to impede analysis while preserving its original functionality. This process inherently involves a trade-off between maximizing the confusion introduced (potency) and minimizing performance degradation (cost), which defines a multi-objective optimization problem. In this study, we propose MOCCO (Multi-Objective Class-based Code Obfuscation), a novel framework that leverages Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithms (MOEAs) to automate and optimize the source code obfuscation process. Our primary contribution is the introduction and integration of class-based obfuscation techniques, which manipulate object-oriented constructs-an aspect often neglected by existing tools. We model obfuscation as a search for optimal solutions on a Pareto front, balancing metrics such as cyclomatic complexity, nesting level, code similarity, and execution time. We implement and compare three distinct MOEAs within our framework, including a global-update adaptation of MOEA/D. Our experimental evaluation, conducted on a set of benchmark programs, demonstrates that our approach, particularly when incorporating class-based techniques, generates code that scores substantially higher on structural-complexity (potency) proxies, with comparable or, in most cases, substantially lower performance overhead, relative to code produced by existing open-source obfuscators under comparable conditions.

title: TCN⁃Transformer: a Method for FBG Bimodal Bionic Tactile Sensing System
authors: Chengang, Lu; Yongqi, Liu; Shuhui, Xing; Huiquan, Lu; Yanxia, Du; Hao, Chen
abstract:
Objective The evolution of embodied intelligence and human-robot collaboration has created an urgent demand for sophisticated tactile perception, enabling machines to interact with the physical world as dexterously and safely as humans. This capability is paramount for applications ranging from robotic-assisted minimally invasive surgery (MIS) and precision assembly to search and rescue in unstructured environments. Among various sensing modalities, fiber Bragg grating (FBG)-based tactile sensing presents a compelling solution due to its inherent advantages: immunity to electromagnetic interference , suitability for harsh environments, and potential for multiplexing and miniaturization. Crucially, a single FBG sensor can simultaneously transduce both static stress and dynamic vibration, mirroring the function of slow-adapting (SA) and fast-adapting (FA) mechanoreceptors in human skin. However, a significant gap exists between the raw potential of FBG sensing and its practical realization in intelligent systems. The core challenge lies in the effective processing of the bimodal signals. Static and dynamic signals possess fundamentally different temporal characteristics, making their feature extraction and fusion non-trivial. Existing algorithms, such as standalone temporal convolutional networks (TCN) or Transformers, often excel in one aspect but falter in another: TCN is adept at capturing local temporal features but may struggle with long-range dependencies, while standard Transformers can model global context but are computationally heavy and may overlook fine-grained local vibration details. Furthermore, practical deployment in robotic systems demands not only high accuracy but also real-time inference and model lightweighting for embedded platforms, a requirement seldom addressed in concert. Therefore, this work is motivated by the necessity to bridge this gap. Its primary objective is to develop and validate a dedicated, efficient neural network architecture that can synergistically decode the bimodal information from a single FBG tactile sensor. The proposed TCN-Transformer hybrid framework aims to achieve robust, high-accuracy material classification (hardness and texture) while maintaining the low latency and compact model size essential for real-time, embedded tactile perception in next-generation robotic systems. Methods To address the aforementioned challenges, we propose a bio-inspired TCN-Transformer fusion network, architected explicitly for FBG bimodal signal processing. The overall system pipeline is depicted in Figure 1. The raw wavelength shifts from a three-channel FBG sensor are first demodulated into static pressure and dynamic vibration signals. These two distinct temporal streams are then processed in parallel by two specialized, lightweight TCN branches before being fused and refined by a streamlined Transformer encoder. The static signal TCN branch is designed for efficiency and focus. It employs depthwise separable convolutions to reduce computational overhead significantly compared to standard convolutions, making it suitable for processing the lower-dimensional but noise-prone static signals. An attention gating mechanism is incorporated immediately after depthwise separable convolutions to allow the network to adaptively weight important temporal features, suppressing irrelevant fluctuations. Conversely, the dynamic signal TCN branch is architected for multi-scale feature extraction to capture the rich, high-frequency content of vibrations.

It utilizes a dual-branch dilated convolution structure: one branch with a larger dilation rate to capture macroscopic vibration patterns, and another with a smaller dilation rate to capture microscopic transient impacts. The outputs are fused and passed through a context enhancement module to ensure coherent integration of multi-scale features. The features from both branches are concatenated to form a unified bimodal representation. This representation is fed into a lightweight, single-layer Transformer Encoder. We adopt a Pre-LayerNorm structure for stable training and incorporate Dropout in both the attention and feed-forward networks for regularization. The Transformer's self-attention mechanism dynamically models the interdependencies between static and dynamic features across the entire sequence, performing a soft, content-aware feature fusion. The final output is projected through a fully connected layer for classification. The model is trained end-to-end using cross-entropy loss. Results and Discussions The proposed TCN-Transformer network was rigorously evaluated on a comprehensive dataset comprising 16 classes of materials with varying hardness and textures. The results demonstrate its superior performance across multiple metrics. First, the model achieved a mean classification accuracy of 95.924 degrees o based on 5-fold cross-validation, with a variance of less than +/- 0.5 degrees o, indicating high robustness and generalizability. This performance significantly outperforms several strong baselines: a CNN-LSTM model (79.236 degrees o ), a pure TCN (85.903 degrees o ), and a pure Transformer (86.837 degrees o ). This decisive margin underscores the effectiveness of the hybrid architecture in leveraging the complementary strengths of both TCN and Transformer components for bimodal signal understanding. Detailed analysis via confusion matrices provides further insight. For hardness classification alone, the model attained an accuracy of 98.54 degrees o, with near-perfect diagonal concentration, confirming the static branch's efficacy in decoding steady-state pressure. For texture classification, accuracy reached 96.25 degrees o. While some confusion exists between textures with similar spectral properties, the model demonstrates a strong capacity to discriminate high-frequency features. The integrated confusion matrix for all 16 classes shows that most errors are confined to samples with the lowest hardness (A0), a challenging case where signal-to-noise ratio is inherently lower, suggesting future work could focus on sensor structure or signal enhancement for very soft materials. Crucially for deployment, the model excels in efficiency. The final optimized model has a compact size of only 4.26 MB. It achieves a single inference latency of 6.3002 ms. This lightweight and fast performance is a direct result of the architectural choices: depthwise separable convolutions, a single Transformer layer, and the removal of redundant components. The attention heatmaps from the Transformer Encoder offer an interpretable view of the model's decision-making. One attention head primarily focuses on local, corresponding time-step correlations, likely aligning static and dynamic features from the same moment. Another head exhibits a more global, diffuse attention pattern, capturing long-range dependencies across the sequence. It validates the design of using multiple attention heads to learn diverse relational strategies between the two modalities.

Conclusions In conclusion, this work presents the TCN-Transformer, a hybrid neural network algorithm designed for processing bimodal tactile signals from a single FBG sensor. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The framework achieves superior classification accuracy for material hardness and texture while meeting the critical requirements of computational efficiency and model lightweighting necessary for embedded deployment. The core innovation lies in its bio-inspired dual-path design, which enables efficient and synergistic processing of static and dynamic tactile modalities. The main contributions of this study are twofold: first, it provides a feasible deep learning solution for the challenging task of FBG-based bimodal signal fusion; second, it demonstrates a practical pathway towards implementing high-fidelity tactile perception in resource-constrained, real-time robotic systems. This work contributes to bridging the gap between sophisticated optical tactile sensing and its practical application in intelligent robots. Future efforts will focus on further optimizing the sensor's performance for extremely soft materials and validating the system in more complex, real-world robotic manipulation tasks.

title: Gender Differences in Test Anxiety During Computer Adaptive Tests in Elementary School
authors: Bruggemann, Thomas; Ludewig, Ulrich; Lorenz, Ramona; McElvany, Nele
abstract: Computer-adaptive tests (CATs) adapt item selection to the student's ability, increasing test efficiency. Unlike fixed item tests (FITs), the solution rate of a CAT is independent of the student's ability. This can interfere with students' expectations about their test performance and increase test anxiety. Since girls tend to report higher levels of trait test anxiety, adaptive testing could have a differential effect on girls' and boys' perceived test anxiety. This study investigates differences in test anxiety between tests administered in FIT or CAT formats. In an experimental within- and between-subject design, the state anxiety of 253 fourth-grade students was measured before, during, and after a reading comprehension test administered either as a FIT or a CAT. Linear mixed-effect models showed that girls reported slightly more state test anxiety at the end of a CAT than boys. Implications for the application of CATs in elementary school classroom settings are discussed.

title: On the Design and Evaluation of Human-Centered Explainable AI Systems: A Systematic Review and Taxonomy
authors: Mangold, Aline; Zietz, Juliane; Weinhold, Susanne; Pannasch, Sebastian
abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes more common in everyday living, there is an increasing demand for intelligent systems that are both performant and understandable. Explainable AI (XAI) systems aim to provide comprehensible explanations of decisions and predictions. At present, however, evaluation processes are rather technical and not sufficiently focused on the needs of human users. Consequently, evaluation studies involving humans can serve as a valuable guide for conducting user studies. This paper presents a comprehensive review of 65 user studies evaluating XAI systems across different domains and application contexts. As a guideline for XAI developers, we provide a holistic overview of the properties of XAI systems and evaluation metrics focused on users (human centered). We propose goals for the human-centered design (design goals) of XAI systems for different user groups (AI novices and data experts). The first part of our results includes the analysis of XAI system characteristics. Importantly, we distinguish between the core system and the XAI explanation, which together form the whole system. Further results include the distinction of evaluation metrics into affection, cognition, usability, interpretability, and explanation metrics. Furthermore, the users, along with their specific characteristics and behavior, can be assessed. For AI novices, the relevant extended design goals include responsibility, acceptance, and user experience. For data experts, the focus is performance oriented, including human-AI collaboration and system task performance. Future literature trends include the design of context-aware and inclusive systems, adapting to users and the situational context. Several limitations in the reviewed literature were identified: a lack of validation, standardization, and documentation; evaluation is focused on particular metrics, rather than holistic; evaluation of explanatory and transparency components of the system is often neglected in user studies. These research gaps could be addressed by integrating existing XAI evaluation frameworks and developing validated questionnaires.

title: Educational series: thermal properties of thermoplastic polymeric materials, experimental and theoretical practices
authors: Ajjagola, Sreecharan; Raji, Ibrahim O.; Weerasinghe, M. A. Sachini N.; Eisenhart, Mary; Konkolewicz, Dominik; Clarkson, Caitlyn M.; Youngblood, Jeffrey P.; Hubbard, Amber M.
abstract: A cornerstone in fundamental polymer processing knowledge remains the thermal properties of polymers and the structure-property-process relationships that culminate in application specific performance. Thermal properties, like the glass transition temperature and melting point, have real world significance and are measured experimentally as they depend on the thermal mechanical history of the material. This educational review introduces the typical experimental methods used to measure the thermal properties of polymers, amorphous and semi-crystalline, and how these properties depend on polymer chemistry and experimental conditions. While not a comprehensive review of all techniques available to characterize polymers, the goal of the present review is to provide sufficient information for a novice to employ commonly available techniques, using best practices, in differential scanning calorimetry, dynamic mechanical analysis, and microscopy. Additionally, introductory theoretical concepts, essential to understanding the observed properties, are also presented to provide context for the experimental methods discussed.

title: Metal-Organic Frameworks-Derived Carbon-Based Materials for Energy Storage and Conversion
authors: Nafees, Amina; Islam, Md. Merajul; Natarajan, Varagunapandiyan
abstract: Carbon compounds generated from metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as exceptionally promising functional materials for enhanced energy storage and conversion, owing to their adjustable porosity, extensive surface area, customizable shape, and plentiful active sites. Most recently published reviews on MOF-derived carbon materials primarily focus on individual aspects such as supercapacitors (SCs), specific electrocatalytic reactions (oxygen reduction reaction ORR/oxygen evolution reaction (OER) or Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER)), synthesis strategies, or catalyst design, resulting in fragmented coverage of the field. In contrast, the present review provides a comprehensive and integrated perspective by systematically correlating material design, synthesis strategies, structure-property relationships, and electrochemical mechanisms across both energy storage (SCs, Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), sodium-ion batteries (SIBs)/KIBs, Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs), and ZABs) and energy conversion (ORR, OER, HER, HOR, CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), and nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR)). Furthermore, it highlights emerging topics-including advanced synthesis routes, operando/in situ characterization, structure-reaction relationships, pilot-scale production, commercialization, and future research directions-that are largely underrepresented in existing reviews. Ultimately, critical challenges and future outlooks are discussed, encompassing the creation of innovative MOF-derived carbon materials, concurrent improvement of catalytic efficiency and stability, a more profound comprehension of internal structure-reaction correlations, the application of operando and in situ characterization techniques, and the advancement of scalable pilot-scale production methods for practical energy applications.

title: Specific Identification Method of Depolarization Enhanced Skin State
abstract:
Objective Polarization sensitive optical coherence tomography is a technique that combines optical coherence tomography with polarization measurement to obtain two-dimensional or three-dimensional depth resolution images of sample intensity and polarization parameters by exploiting the low coherence characteristics of the light source. Due to its potential to obtain more comprehensive information on biological tissue structures, it has currently been applied in the diagnosis and monitoring of eye diseases, burn and scar skin, tendon and myelinated nerve fiber lesions, atherosclerosis, breast tumors, etc. However, the combination of polarization theory and optical coherence tomography is difficult to be widely used due to its complex information, low specificity and poor readability. From the perspective of exploring the specific analysis method of tissue polarization information, this paper combines the multiple parameter theory of depolarization mechanism and the Mueller matrix classification theory to define a specific pointer parameter group, which can efficiently and accurately characterize early skin lesions. Methods In this study, firstly, the expressions of multiple polarization parameters with clear physical meanings containing elements of the Mueller matrix are summarized. One set of parameters is derived based on the light propagation model, while the other set of polarization parameters is derived by establishing the relationship between the component matrix of the classical decomposition of the macroscopic Mueller matrix and the component matrix of the polar decomposition based on its unique form. On this basis, on the one hand, six combined parameters obtained by classifying and combining 14 polarization parameters derived from two methods, namely the light propagation model and the unique form exploration of regular decomposition, are introduced. By combining multiple types of depolarizing parameters with the expressions of non-depolarizing parameters, a method for enhancing the contrast mechanism considering the depolarizing mechanism is obtained. On the other hand, the polarization degree and statistical analysis theory are studied and the general classification form of the Mueller matrix is given. The arrow form of the Mueller matrix containing statistical parameters is characterized under specific conditions of different polarization degree values. The RVC parameters including the variance in the form of classification arrows of the experimental Mueller matrix are obtained to characterize the polarization characteristics of the tissue. Finally, the specific parameter RVC obtained by the Mueller matrix classification based on the arrow representation method is combined with the multiple polarization parameters obtained by the depolarization mechanism considered method as D Delta e-com, alpha epsilon(d Delta e-com), R Delta e-com, and alpha epsilon(r Delta e-com). Four depolarization enhanced specific recognition parameters, DRVC Delta e-com, alpha epsilon(RVCd Delta e-com), RRVC Delta e-com and alpha epsilon(RVCr Delta e-com) are then obtained to characterize the diattenuation and birefringence and their axis. In order to demonstrate the application potential of the proposed method, parametric images of mouse skin under different conditions are obtained using a built polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT).

Results and Discussions The PS-OCT system, imaging principle and depth-resolved polarization imaging process are shown. It highlights the system structure, sample preparation, data acquisition and analysis processes. Under four different incident conditions of polarized light, the image information of 16 elements in the Mueller matrix within the effective imaging depth of the sample is obtained by using the PS-OCT system. Then, the corresponding multiple polarization parameter images, RVC parameter image and specific recognition parameter images are calculated. Furthermore, the region of interest is determined and the image analysis is completed. The sample preparation process is based on isolated normal skin tissues in the resting phase and inflammatory fibrotic skin tissues of mouse, which are fixed with paraformaldehyde and stored in a laboratory-specific refrigerator. The analysis shows that for isolated normal and inflammatory skin samples of mice, the proposed method not only improves the contrast of RVC images, but also retains the characteristics of superior depth contrast performance, high sensitivity to specific structures, and high integration of polarization information. It also has the significant potential of depolarization parameters to enhance and smooth the contrast of the entire imaging depth, indicate skin dehydration phenomena, be sensitive to changes in the micro-structure of the skin surface, and identify the boundaries of deep skin tissue structures. Conclusions Based on PS-OCT technology, this paper conducts research on a specific recognition method for depolarization enhanced skin structure states, aiming to achieve accurate and efficient assessment of skin tissue structure states and their changes. Combining a method of enhancing the polarization contrast of isolated mouse skin by PS-OCT considering the depolarizing mechanism, and a multi-state specific recognition method of skin tissue structure based on the Mueller matrix classification theory, a set of depolarizing enhanced skin structure state-specific parameters is proposed. The specific parameter images of the depolarizing enhanced skin structure state of isolated mouse skin, including normal skin tissue in the resting phase and inflammatory fibrotic skin tissue, are obtained and calculated using the PS-OCT system established in the laboratory. The experimental results show that the proposed method has the characteristics of superior depth contrast performance, high sensitivity to specific structures, and high integration of polarization information. At the same time, it also has the important potential to improve and smooth the depth contrast of the entire imaging, indicate skin dehydration phenomena, be sensitive to changes in the micro-structure of the skin surface, and identify the boundaries of deep skin tissue structures.

title: Adaptation and Psychometric Validation of a Family, Teacher, and Peer Support Questionnaire in Primary Education Using Visual and Auditory Supports
authors: Lara, Laura; Saracostti, Mahia; de-Toro, Ximena
venue: ELECTRONIC JOURNAL OF RESEARCH IN EDUCATIONAL PSYCHOLOGY
abstract: Introduction. Perceived support from family, teachers, and peers is a central component of school adjustment in primary education. The aim of this study was to adapt and examine the psychometric properties of a brief questionnaire designed to assess family, teacher, and peer support among 3rd-and 4th-grade students in Chile, incorporating illustrations, pictorial response scales, and auditory resources to ensure accessibility. Method. The adaptation process included item redesign, expert judgment, and focus groups with students. The final version was administered to 471 students in third grade (53.7%) and fourth grade (46.3%) of Primary Education, aged 7 to 11 years (M = 8.77, SD = 0.71) (non-probabilistic sampling; 51% boys and 49% girls), using a computer-based application with integrated audio. Descriptive analyses and a confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) were conducted. Results. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a three-factor correlated structure (family, teacher, and peer support) with adequate fit indices (RMSEA = .046; CFI = .971; TLI = .967). The three subscales demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency (ordinal alpha = .78-.89) and showed predictive validity with respect to academic performance. Conclusion. Overall, the results indicate that the questionnaire is a valid, reliable, and developmentally appropriate tool for assessing perceived support in Primary Education. Its application facilitates the early identification of support needs and informs educational and preventive practices within schools. These findings provide empirical evidence for the measurement of contextual factors in early grades and support its use in educational screening and intervention aimed at improving students' school adjustment.

title: An Efficient and Fast Image Encryption Scheme Based on a Novel One-Dimensional Hybrid Chaotic System
authors: Terchoune, Fatma Zohra; Mehallel, Elhadi; Rabehi, Abdelhalim; Agajie, Takele Ferede; Khlifi, Mohamed Arbi; Rabehi, Abdelaziz
abstract: Recently, images have been used widely in a variety of fields, including social media, the military and medicine. Sensitive images are often transmitted over insecure networks and chaotic maps offer effective cryptographic properties for securing these transmissions. One-dimensional (1D) chaotic maps are commonly employed in data encryption due to their simplicity, high randomness properties, excellent chaotic behaviours and high security levels. However, numerous chaos-based image encryption algorithms have drawbacks that are generally related to the chaotic systems used and their encryption structures. To overcome these limitations, this paper first proposes a hybrid chaotic system based on 1D-sine-logistic-sine-tent (1D-SLST) chaotic maps. Using 1D-SLST chaotic generators, we produced a new 1D chaotic map exhibiting enhanced chaotic properties compared to the conventional maps. To examine its application in multimedia security, an effective image encryption algorithm is also introduced that leverages the chaotic behaviour of 1D-SLST. Our algorithm utilises a variety of confusion operations, including zigzag transform, image rotation and pixel confusion. A pixel adaptive diffusion operation based on modulo arithmetic is also introduced. Simulation experiments and security performance evaluations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, which gives information entropy, NPCR and UACI values of 7.998866, 99.60876% and 33.46990%, respectively, which are close to ideal values. Comparative simulation results indicate that the proposed image encryption algorithm ensures a high level of security and fast encryption speed, achieving superior performance compared to several state-of-the-art methods.

title: A Task-Specific Performance Rating Scale for Laparoscopic Intracorporeal Suturing and Knot Tying: Development and Initial Evaluation
authors: Xia, Xiang; Zhou, Zihan; Lu, Yihong; Bian, Zhengqian; Tang, Qiushi; Zhang, Zizhen
venue: JOURNAL OF LAPAROENDOSCOPIC & ADVANCED SURGICAL TECHNIQUES
abstract: Background: Laparoscopic intracorporeal suturing and knot tying is a core minimally invasive surgical skill, but generic global rating instruments may not identify the task-specific technical errors needed for targeted feedback. We developed an 8-item performance rating scale for a standardized simulator task and evaluated its measurement properties. Methods: In a cross-sectional cohort, 82 participants across 5 training levels completed 1 interrupted laparoscopic suture consisting of 1 needle pass, 3 intracorporeal knots, and final cutting. Deidentified videos were independently scored by 3 raters. Interrater reliability was estimated using 2-way random effects, absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Between-level performance was assessed using Kruskal-Wallis tests, Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons, and Spearman correlation. Twelve learners completed the task before and after standardized training. Results: Quality scores differed across training levels (P < .001) and correlated strongly with level (Spearman rho = 0.872, P < .001). Completion time decreased with level (rho = -0.897, P < .001). Total-score reliability was excellent (ICC[2,1] = 0.960; ICC[2,3] = 0.986). After training, mean quality score increased by 5.83 points, and completion time decreased by 29.17 seconds (both P < .001). Conclusions: The scale provides a reliable, reproducible method for video-based assessment of laparoscopic intracorporeal suturing and knot-tying performance. Its principal current use is to differentiate novice and early-stage operators and to track progress during simulator-based practice. More demanding tasks and multicenter evaluation are needed before use for advanced proficiency decisions.

title: Developing prediction model for ripeness level of melon (Cucumis melo L.) based on acoustic impulses using artificial neural network (ANN)
abstract: Non-climacteric fruits such as melons are often difficult to assess for ripeness due to the lack of obvious physical changes upon ripeness. Currently, melon producers rely on visual assessment, which requires specialized expertise and involves inefficient, destructive test methods. Thus, a non-destructive approach like acoustic impulse is crucial for ripeness classification. This study aims to develop a melon ripeness prediction model based on an acoustic impulse test. A total of 120 Honey Globe melons (Cucumis melo var. inodorus) were measured for acoustic properties (dominant frequency, magnitude, zero moment power, and short-term energy), using a knocker to obtain acoustic parameter data. The acoustic parameter data were processed using an artificial neural network (ANN) with the Backpropagation method, and model performance was evaluated using a confusion matrix. The model showed excellent performance with an R2 value of 94.46% and accuracy, precision, and recall rates of 98.33%, 97.37%, and 97.37%, respectively.

title: Kinetic and Simulation Study of Methane Stepwise Conversion with CO for Clean Fuel Production
authors: Yu, Hanzhi; Yang, Shiying; Mei, Lixinyu; Weng, Yixin; Jiao, Fan; Liu, Qibin
abstract: Dry methane reforming (DMR) is a promising pathway for clean fuel production owing to its capability to convert CO2 into value-added carbon monoxide. However, its practical deployment is plagued by catalyst deactivation from carbon deposition and high activation energy barriers. Methane carbon cyclic reforming (MCCR) enables in situ removal of deposited carbon by coupling catalytic decomposition of methane (CDM) with the reverse Boudouard (RB) reaction, thereby generating H2 and CO with favorable selectivity. This makes MCCR a potential pathway for clean fuel synthesis. The development of numerical models has been hampered by the lack of understanding of the dynamics of MCCR, allowing key aspects such as kinetic response to remain in a state of confusion. In this study, a kinetic model for MCCR over commercial Ni/Al2O3 catalysts has been established. Apparent activation energies for CDM and RB are quantified under varying experimental conditions, and a numerical model is introduced to characterize the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of MCCR. Over 200 carbon deposition-removal cycles, the timely elimination of low-graphitized carbon enables a carbon removal efficiency of 99.73%, highlighting the catalyst's stability under cyclic operation. Compared with conventional DMRs, the stepwise pathway of CDM and RB reduces the apparent activation energies by 76.41% and 18.83%, respectively, in the temperature range of 948 K-1023K. The simulation results agree with experimental conversion data and provide insights into distributions of velocity, pressure, and species during the reforming process. These findings offer theoretical insights and quantitative support for design and experiment of MCCR.

title: Large Language Models as Distributional Baselines for Language Tasks
authors: Trott, Sean; Michaelov, James; Jones, Cameron; Chang, Tyler; Bergen, Benjamin
abstract: In order to ask questions about the mechanisms underpinning human cognition, researchers must control for properties of stimuli that could confound detected effects. In experiments involving linguistic stimuli, this includes properties like frequency, length, and neighborhood size of those stimuli, which are known to affect behavioral and neural responses. With improvements in the performance and usability of language models, it is now possible to also control for how predictable stimuli and their parts are, on the basis of the distributions of words alone: their distributional predictability. This coincides with a resurgence of interest in the possibility that statistical language learning may underlie a broad range of human cognitive phenomena; indeed, there are both theoretical and empirical reasons to believe that humans rely on distributional information during certain cognitive tasks. This creates a confound, whereby experimental operationalizations of psychological constructs with linguistic stimuli may not in fact be testing what they are intended to test. Thus, the central contributions of this paper are twofold: first, we articulate the conditions under which distributional predictability threatens the internal validity of an experiment; and second, we provide concrete recommendations for how to control for this potential confound. Beyond these primary contributions, we survey techniques for measuring distributional predictability, review theoretical and empirical work supporting the role of distributional statistics in human cognition, and present several case studies illustrating the range of possible outcomes-from the "distributional baselines" only marginally affecting theoretical inferences to constituting fully deflationary confounds. We also enumerate and address potential objections to this approach. This paper is primarily intended for researchers in psychology, cognitive science, and linguistics who use linguistic stimuli but have not yet incorporated distributional baselines into their work.

title: Industrial Internet-Oriented Unsupervised Hydro-Turbine Bearing Fault Diagnosis via Prototype-Disentangled Conditional Wasserstein Domain Adaptation
authors: Li, Xueyi; Hu, Binghao; Dong, Jiannan; Dong, Zhilin
abstract: With the rapid development of Industrial Internet-oriented smart energy systems, hydro-turbine generator units are increasingly monitored through networked sensors, industrial communication infrastructures, and edge/cloud-based condition-monitoring platforms. These Internet-connected monitoring environments provide abundant vibration data for intelligent operation and maintenance (O&M) but also introduce a challenging unsupervised cross-scenario diagnosis problem. Specifically, diagnostic models trained on labeled historical data may suffer severe performance degradation when deployed to unlabeled online data collected under different hydraulic conditions, rotational speeds, or operating conditions. Furthermore, existing domain adaptation methods, in their pursuit of distribution alignment, frequently overlook a critical bottleneck that limits generalization performance: inter-class entanglement. Specifically, under intense hydraulic background noise and cross-condition distribution shifts, features belonging to distinct fault types are highly susceptible to aliasing within the feature space. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes a Conditional Wasserstein Adversarial Network with Bi-level Prototype Disentanglement Regularization (CWAN-BPDR). First, a Conditional Wasserstein Adversarial Network (CWAN) is constructed by combining the smooth-gradient property of Wasserstein distance with conditional adversarial alignment, thereby achieving stable and fine-grained category-level domain adaptation. Furthermore, to alleviate the inter-class entanglement problem that may arise during cross-domain alignment, a Bi-level Prototype Disentanglement Regularization (BPDR) term is designed. By jointly implementing source-target prototype alignment and prototype-feature bidirectional alignment, BPDR explicitly suppresses inter-class confusion and enhances intra-class compactness and inter-class separability in the feature space. Experimental results on the JNU and NEFU datasets demonstrate that CWAN-BPDR achieves average diagnostic accuracies of 97.82% and 98.99%, respectively, while significantly mitigating label entanglement in challenging cross-operating-condition tasks. These results indicate that the proposed method can effectively transfer diagnostic knowledge acquired from labeled historical operating conditions to unlabeled online monitoring data. It can therefore serve as an offline-trained diagnostic module for Industrial Internet of Things-based condition-monitoring platforms in hydropower systems.

title: Emotion Recognition Using Acoustic Features and Deep Learning: A Speaker-Independent Study
authors: Kolodziej, Marcin; Majkowski, Andrzej; Rywik, Tomasz
abstract: This study compares the effectiveness of two approaches to speech emotion recognition for three affective states in Polish: sad, neutral, and happy. Both a set of acoustic features-capturing prosodic, phonatory, temporal, spectral, and cepstral properties-and representations learned by self-supervised models (wav2vec 2.0 and WavLM) were analyzed. Experiments were conducted on the nEMO corpus, comprising 2327 recordings from nine speakers, using a rigorous leave-one-subject-out protocol to evaluate cross-speaker generalization. In the feature-based approach, 107 acoustic features were used, and classification was performed with logistic regression and, additionally, SVM variants. In the deep learning approach, the wav2vec2-base and WavLM-base models were fine-tuned for the three-class task. The best results were achieved by the self-supervised models: WavLM reached a global balanced accuracy of 0.727 and a macro-F1 score of 0.710, while wav2vec 2.0 achieved 0.722 and 0.695, respectively. Both outperformed the feature-based approach (BAcc = 0.627, macro-F1 = 0.584). Confusion matrix analysis showed that the greatest difficulty lies in distinguishing the neutral class from the sad and happy classes, whereas sad and happy classes are more clearly separable. Feature utility analysis (SFS under the LOSO protocol) indicated the significant role of cepstral features (MFCCs and their derivatives), complemented by selected prosodic and temporal features. An additional comparison of SVM classifiers suggested that the main limitation of this approach lies in the signal representation itself rather than solely in the choice of classifier. Explainability analyses of the deep models, using layer-wise probing and integrated gradients, showed that affective information is best represented in intermediate layers, and that model decisions rely on locally salient segments of the signal. Furthermore, a speaker adaptation experiment demonstrated that personalization significantly improves classification performance, highlighting the potential of such methods for long-term monitoring of affective expression changes in the same individual.

title: Extracting and clustering human visual strategies from video gaze data with Hidden Markov Models for Video-QA performance understanding
authors: Joutei, Badr Tahri; Le-Callet, Patrick; Bruckert, Alexandre; Dolle, Laurent
venue: 2025 13TH EUROPEAN WORKSHOP ON VISUAL INFORMATION PROCESSING, EUVIP
abstract:
Human gaze patterns during tasked viewing of an action offer insights into human attention, intention recognition, and the cognitive state of the viewer. These insights have applications in many domains such as collaborative robotics, user interface design, and medical assessment.

In this work, we demonstrate an association between visual strategies employed during task-driven viewing and performance in video question answering (Video-QA). To do so, we leverage eye-tracking data to analyze human visual strategies during action recognition. Specifically, we record participants' gaze as they watch demonstrations of short atomic actions, which form a basis to describe all long form actions, followed by a question-answering step to assess their comprehension.

We model the spatio-temporal dynamics of gaze behavior using Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and cluster visual strategies for demonstrations of the same task based on visual behavior similarity. We use Binomial Generalized Linear Mixed Model (BGLMM) to investigate how this behavior relates to Video-QA performance. Our results show that participants who exhibit specific visual strategies, as well as participants who are consistent in their visual strategy across different videos, perform better on the question-answering task, while other visual strategies are associated with poor performance and can reveal misunderstandings of the questions. Specifically, more dynamic gaze behavior, with more focused fixations on a relevant object, and more relevant objects considered in the scene are all properties of a better performing visual strategy.

By identifying gaze patterns associated with Video-QA performance, using a probabilistic Bayesian method with interpretable learnable parameters, our approach enables clearer insights into human perception, potentially contributing to more robust and efficient action recognition machine learning models.

title: SpkAugTSE: A Simple and Efficient Approach to Address Target Confusion in End-to-End Speaker Extraction
authors: You, Zhenghai; Zhou, Zhenyu; Li, Lantian; Wang, Dong
venue: 2025 ASIA PACIFIC SIGNAL AND INFORMATION PROCESSING ASSOCIATION ANNUAL SUMMIT AND CONFERENCE, APSIPA ASC
abstract: Target confusion, defined as occasional switching to non-target speakers, poses a key challenge for end-to-end speaker extraction (E2E-SE) systems. We argue that this problem is largely caused by the lack of generalizability and discrimination of the speaker embeddings, and introduce a simple yet effective speaker augmentation strategy to tackle the problem. Specifically, we propose a time-domain resampling and rescaling pipeline that alters speaker traits while preserving other speech properties. This generates a variety of pseudo-speakers to help establish a generalizable speaker embedding space, while the speaker-trait-specific augmentation creates hard samples that force the model to focus on genuine speaker characteristics. Experiments on WSJ02Mix and LibriMix show that our method mitigates the target confusion and improves extraction performance. Moreover, it can be combined with metric learning, another effective approach to address target confusion, leading to further gains.

title: Learning Mathematical Vectors' Properties and Operations Using the LSEESC Methodology in Engineering and Science Students
authors: Sanchez Guzman, Daniel; Cervantes Juarez, Erika
venue: 2025 IEEE FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION CONFERENCE, FIE
abstract: In this research-to-practice WIP full work, we investigated the impact of the learning process on the vector's definition and operation concepts utilizing the Learning Science and Engineering with Electronic Spreadsheet Cycle (LSEESC) methodology. This approach was adopted because of the numerous physics courses at different engineering academic programs, students' difficulty in understanding the mathematical models in learning physics is one of the primary factors influencing students' academic low performance. For enhanced the vectors' comprehension, we selected the Free-Body Diagram Analysis (FBDA), as it is the fundamental approach for understanding dynamics with forces and masses interactions. The study was conducted with N = 140 students, taking courses in the first and second semesters, and being the first course of physics in both cases. In the lecture sessions, electronic spreadsheets were used to describe the operations of vector subtraction and addition, also these are used in the practice reports and experiments. For analyzing the impact in the learning process, we employed as quantitative tools the Normalized Conceptual Gain (NCG), Concentration Factor (CF), and Rasch's Index (RI), and for a qualitative analysis, the Semantic Differential (SD) was implemented to ascertain the students' perceptions of the learning experience. Before and after the learning sequence, students answered the Test of Understanding of Vectors (TUV) as pre- and post-test for measuring in a quantitative manner the concepts addressed and learned, and at the conclusion they complete the semantic differential test to collect the perceptions about the learning sequence.

title: Analysis of a Generative AI-Based Graphical Learning Assistance Tool in IPR Courses
authors: Yen, Chen-Chieh; Hsieh, Pei-Tsen; Chen, Yu-Chieh; Chang, Chia-Kai
venue: 2025 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON ADVANCED LEARNING TECHNOLOGIES, ICALT
abstract: This study develops dAIgram, a generative AI-assisted learning platform that integrates automatic visual diagram generation, quiz creation, and interactive Q&A to help students transform large volumes of text into intuitive visuals, enhancing comprehension and application of complex content. It supports various data formats, including PDFs, videos, and text files. An experiment with 76 students from an Intellectual Property Right (IPR) course examined its impact, revealing a significant improvement between midterm and final scores, with an average increase of 6.23% for all students and 9.2% for science and engineering students. Visual diagrams, adaptive quizzes, and interactive Q&A effectively strengthened comprehension, while machine learning analysis showed that platform activity data could predict quiz performance with 3.04% RMSE. Humanities students benefited more from ChatGPT Q&A, whereas science and engineering students showed greater improvement when using the visual diagram generation model. Additionally, survey results indicate that dAIgram reduces learning anxiety and increases engagement. These findings highlight its effectiveness in enhancing learning outcomes and its potential applications in large-volume textual content education. Future research can explore dAIgram's applicability across different disciplines, evaluating its broader educational impact.

title: Validity and Reliability of the 3-Dimensional Printed PhysioCode Handheld Dynamometer for Knee Muscle Strength Assessment
authors: Sabino, George Schayer; Nascimento, Diego Henrique Antunes; Madaleno, Fernanda Oliveira; Vimieiro, Claysson Bruno Santos; Costa, Pollyana Helena Vieira; Araujo, Guilherme Augusto Santos; Ferreira, Matheus Hissa Lourenco; Resende, Renan Alves
abstract: Context: Handheld dynamometry is common for isometric strength testing, but the high cost and import barriers of commercial devices (eg, MicroFET II) limit access. Three-dimensional (3D) printing enables low-cost, customizable instruments. We developed the 3D-printed PhysioCode and examined its measurement properties for knee strength. Design: Methods and Technical Report evaluating concurrent validity and test-retest reliability versus a reference handheld dynamometer. Methods: Forty-nine healthy adults (23.2 [3.9] y; body mass index 21.9 [2.8] kg/m2) performed 3 isometric trials of dominant-limb knee extension and flexion with both devices in randomized order, assessed by 2 trained novice raters under blinded analysis. Concurrent validity was evaluated using Pearson correlation coefficients (r) and root mean square error, and agreement between devices was assessed using Bland-Altman analyses. Reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC[2,1] and ICC[2,k]), along with the standard error of measurement and minimal detectable change at 95% confidence. We compared single and repeated test strategies. Results: All mean values differed by <= 21 N between devices across knee extensors and flexors. Concurrent validity was strong-very strong (r= .88-.95; P <.001), with lower root mean square error for averaged repetitions. Bland-Altman showed small, direction-specific bias: PhysioCode slightly overestimated extensor force values (-17 to 21 N) and underestimated flexor force values (-12 N). Reliability was excellent: PhysioCode ICC(2,1) = .93 to .95 and ICC(2,k) = .98 to .98; MicroFET II ICC(2,1) = .89 to .94 and ICC(2, k) = .96 to .98. Averaging 2 to 3 trials reduced standard error of measurement and minimal detectable change at 95% confidence relative to single trials or maxima. Conclusions: The 3D-printed PhysioCode showed adequate concurrent validity and excellent test-retest reliability for knee extensor/flexor strength, with performance comparable to the MicroFET II in this sample of young, healthy adults. Averaging 2 or 3 repetitions improved precision. These findings suggest that PhysioCode may represent an option for strength assessment, warranting further evaluation in target clinical populations.

title: Validation of versatile training tissue based on konjac powder materials as a surgical training model
authors: Hiki, Ruriko; Tanaka, Ryota; Ishii, Shun; Kojima, Yohei; Kishiki, Tomokazu; Kaneda, Ryo; Nakazato, Yoko
abstract: Purpose Simulation-based surgical training is becoming increasingly important. However, dry laboratory materials lack tissue realism, whereas wet laboratory training raises ethical and cost concerns. We investigated Versatile Training Tissue (VTT), a konjac glucomannan-based model designed to solve problems. This study validated the use of VTT as an educational tool for surgical simulation.Methods Twenty physicians, including 10 expert surgeons and 10 novice residents, performed dissection, ligation, excision, and suturing using the VTT (VESSEL-IN TYPE). The participants' performance was evaluated by three blinded specialist surgeons using four items extracted from the Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills. Additionally, evaluations were conducted based on the measured procedural time and wound dehiscence area.Results The expert group showed significantly better performances than the novice group in terms of the modified Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills (14.0 vs. 8.7 points, P = 0.007), procedural time (455.5 vs. 891.6 s, P = 0.002), and wound dehiscence area, representing a 58% reduction (4.12 vs. 9.92 mm2, P = 0.039, Cohen's d = 1.025).Conclusions The VTT demonstrated construct validity as an objective assessment tool for surgical training, offering realistic tissue properties. Our results suggest that VTT could be used as a simulation model for surgical training.

title: A High-Readability and Image-Integrated QR Code Generation Method
venue: RECENT CHALLENGES IN INTELLIGENT INFORMATION AND DATABASE SYSTEMS, ACIIDS 2026, PT I
abstract: This research presents an aesthetic and readable QR Code beautification method that embeds image information into QR Codes in a structured manner, achieving natural visual fusion while preserving stable scanning performance. The proposed approach exploits the linear properties of Reed-Solomon (RS) codes to redistribute data and error-correction symbols. By constructing an RS extension matrix via Gaussian-Jordan elimination, the control bits originally located at the QR Code center are remapped to peripheral modules, producing results that maintain both data robustness and visual alignment. To enhance visual quality, the QR Code is partitioned into central and peripheral regions. The central modules are rendered using circular elements with an 8-pixel diameter and are further refined through brightness and color adjustments, maximizing retention of the original image details. In contrast, the peripheral modules preserve the traditional black-and-white structure to ensure decoding stability. For improved recognizability, the system automatically adjusts brightness based on grayscale balance and the contribution of each RGB channel, applying weighted corrections when the available dynamic range becomes limited. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances the visual appeal and perceptual integration of QR Codes while maintaining a high scanning success rate. The overall design is compatible, reproducible, and provides a practical technical foundation for the generation and application of visually enriched QR Codes.

title: Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Properties of the Turkish Version of the Dementia Literacy Assessment (DeLA)
authors: Yilmaz, Fikriye; Ozcan, Emre; Ozcan, Deniz Gungor
abstract: Introduction: This study aims to culturally adapt the Dementia Literacy Assessment (DeLA) scale into Turkish and to evaluate its psychometric properties. The DeLA introduces an innovative approach by employing narrative-based storytelling, rather than conventional didactic methods, to assess dementia literacy and to challenge prevailing societal misconceptions. Methods: The study comprised procedures including linguistic equivalence testing, expert consensus (ICC = 0.88), and readability analysis. The sample consisted of 120 participants (mean age: 60.88 +/- 8.72 years). Participants completed a pre-test, read two culturally adapted stories, and subsequently completed a post-test. Psychometric evaluation included KR-20 reliability coefficients and corrected item-total correlations. Results: The mean DeLA score increased significantly from 7.71 +/- 1.95 to 8.54 +/- 1.99 (p < 0.05), corresponding to an overall improvement of 14%. The greatest increase was observed among male participants (25.01%). Correct response rates to the statement that "forgetfulness is a normal part of aging" improved by 47.3%. The scale demonstrated good internal consistency, with KR-20 values of 0.701 (pre-test) and 0.734 (post-test). Education level, family history of dementia, and caregiving experience were significantly associated with higher post-test performance (p < 0.05). Discussion: Narrative-based assessments such as the DeLA may bridge gaps in dementia knowledge more effectively than traditional approaches by directly addressing deeply rooted cultural myths, including the normalization of forgetfulness. Conclusion: The Turkish version of the DeLA is a valid and reliable instrument with high sensitivity for assessing dementia literacy. Its narrative-based format effectively challenges deeply ingrained cultural misconceptions.
